key_insight: A metallic microstructure and texture can be used to infer the alloy recipe and processing conditions, and simple conventional descriptors outperform learned embeddings for this reverse-design task.
engineering_relevance: This enables data-driven back-calculation of likely alloy compositions and extrusion settings from observed structures, supporting faster alloy/process development and troubleshooting.
method: Built a dataset of 107 magnesium alloy extrusion cases across 14 alloys with optical micrographs and X-ray texture measurements.
Compared three structure descriptors: conventional grain/texture statistics, pretrained image embeddings, and a graph neural network on grain networks.
Paired each descriptor with prediction heads for composition-from-process (Task A) and process-from-composition (Task B).
evidence_signal: Under 5-fold cross-validation, conventional descriptors identified the correct alloy in 65% of held-out cases, versus 17% for always predicting the most common alloy, and they reduced process-temperature error relative to composition alone.
watch_item: The dataset is small and discretized, so performance may not transfer well to continuous process spaces or broader alloy families.
paper_title: Which alloy composition,what process parameters? Inferring the recipe from optimized metallic microstructure and texture
